function_v0.name: execute_strategy

function_v0.doc:
Same as [`Self::execute_strategy`] but pulls **multiple** seed tokens from
the user before running any step.

# Why this exists

A constant-product LP deposit (Aquarius) requires both pool tokens present
in the executor before the `AddLiquidity` step runs. The existing
`execute_strategy` pulls exactly one seed token, which forces a prior swap
step \xe2\x80\x94 but routing a Soroswap swap through the executor exceeds the 100M
CPU instruction budget (~105M measured). Splitting into a direct Soroswap
call (~35M) followed by this multi-seed entry point (~55M) keeps both
transactions comfortably within limits.

# Invariants

Identical to `execute_strategy`: I1, I3, I4, I8, I11. The only difference
is pulling N tokens instead of 1 before step execution begins.

# Seeds

Each [`Seed`] names a token and an amount. All are pulled from the user in
one pass before the first step reads any balance. The sweep set includes
every seed token, so nothing can be stranded.
function_v0.name: execute_strategy_multi_seed

udt_error_enum_v0.doc:
`fort-strategy-executor` errors.

# Two ranges, one enum

A contract can only return one error type, but the vault's failures come from
two places: its own logic, and the `fort-common` primitives it builds on.
Rather than collapse every common failure into a single opaque variant \xe2\x80\x94 which
would give twenty distinct conditions one identity \xe2\x80\x94 the common codes are
mirrored here **with their original numeric values**.

So `Error(Contract, #20)` means "paused" whether it was raised by
`fort_common::pause` or by anything else in the system, and an integrator
learns one code per condition rather than one per layer.

`test::access::common_error_codes_are_mirrored_exactly` asserts the numbers
agree. Codes 300\xe2\x80\x93399 are this contract's own, per the map in
`fort_common::error`.

udt_struct_v0.doc:
One leg of a strategy.

# Two divergences from the port prompt's shape, both deliberate

The prompt specifies `Step { adapter, action, token_in, amount_fixed, bps,
data: Bytes }`.

- `data: Bytes` becomes [`AdapterParams`]. ADR-006: a closed
`#[contracttype]` enum is validated by the host at the XDR boundary, so
there is no decode step and therefore no panic path. An opaque blob would
reintroduce the entire "fallible decode of caller-supplied bytes" finding
class that the rest of this codebase does not have.
- `amount_fixed` plus `bps` becomes one [`StepAmount`]. Two fields encoding
one choice invites the state where both are set, and every caller then has
to know which wins.
